rows.note: This is the all-purpose polite address for an adult man, especially in service or formal situations.

example.english: Sir, please sign for this document.
example.traditional: 先生，麻煩你簽收呢份文件。
example.jyutping: sin1 saang1 maa4 faan4 nei5 cim1 sau1 ni1 fan6 man4 gin6

rows.note: Choose this more colloquial form when addressing an unfamiliar man informally.

example.english: Sir, excuse me, is someone sitting here?
example.traditional: 阿生，借借，個位有人坐㗎喎。
example.jyutping: aa3 saang1 ze3 ze3 go3 wai2 jau5 jan4 co5 gaa3 wo3

rows.note: Use this formal military term when addressing a superior officer in an explicitly military setting.

example.english: Sir, the report is complete; please give orders.
example.jyutping: zoeng2 gun1 bou3 gou3 jyun4 sing4 cing2 zi2 si6

rows.note: Use this Hong Kong police or uniformed-service slang form for addressing a superior officer, not an ordinary adult man.

example.english: Sir, there is a fight up ahead!
example.jyutping: aa3 se4 cin4 min6 jau5 jan4 daa2 gaau1
